newsitem.title: UK: UNHCR to up Zaire cargo relief flights on demand.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR to up Zaire cargo relief flights on demand.

text.p: U.N. refugee agency UNHCR, which has been operating relief flights between Entebbe, Uganda, and Kisangani, Zaire, since April 12, said it will increase capacity when it is required.
Rodney Albro, responsible for UNHCR logistics and airline control, told Reuters in a telephone interview from Geneva that each flight had been transporting up to 45 tonnes of supplies.
"We have been carrying vehicles from Japan and Korea and shipments including plastic sheeting, jerry cans and blankets from western Europe and Poland," he said.

UNHCR has used a Russian built IL-76 freighter, owned by Inversia Airlines of Latvia and contracted via UK air cargo broker AirRep. Return flights had been bringing up to 200 Rwandan refugees out of Kisangani either to Goma in Zaire or the Rwandan capital of Kigali.

"The aircraft is insured for passenger-carrying purposes and is equipped with a walk-on/walk-off ramp," he said, adding that up to two round-trips a day had been operated since April 12 on a six-days-a-week basis.

"We are having to use the small Kisangani military airfield at present as the international airport there is closed, reportedly due to mining. We hope it will re-open over the next few days and this give us much better operational options," said Albro.
He said that UNHCR could add a second aircraft to its Zaire relief operation "within 24 hours" as and when necessary, but he thought this was not required immediately.

"Apart from our aircraft, there is other (relief aircraft) capacity in the region," he said, noting that other agencies involved in the relief operation included the U.N. World Food Programme, U.N. children's fund UNICEF and international relief group Medicins Sans Frontieres (MSF).
